subject: ventures/security-deposit-return-calculator
professional: a landlord-tenant attorney or residential property manager who settles move-out deposits; first checks: is the prorated rent for a full or partial month exactly rent x days / days-in-month, does the statement satisfy the state's itemization rule (CA Civ. Code 1950.5(g): itemized statement within 21 days, receipts or invoices for deductions of $125 or more; NY GOL 7-108(1-a)(e): itemized statement within 14 days of vacating or the landlord forfeits any right to retain any portion; TX Prop. Code 92.103-92.104: refund and written description of deductions within 30 days of surrender), is interest computed the way the statute says (NY GOL 7-103(2-a): six or more units, interest less a 1% per annum administration fee; MA c.186 s.15B: 5% or the bank's rate), and does the statement carry the dates and parties that prove it was timely

evidence.correctness: Ran computeDepositSettlement, computeDepositInterest and computeProratedRent via node -e. Deposit side recomputes exactly by hand: $1,500 less $180 + $45 = $1,275 refund; $1,000 deposit against $1,400 unpaid rent = $400 balance owed; MA c.186 s.15B(3)(b) 5% statutory rate on $1,500 held 365 days = $75.00 (observed 75). Proration is wrong whenever rent/days is not a whole cent: the code rounds the daily rate to cents and then multiplies, so a full 31-day month at $1,850 bills $1,850.08 (59.68 x 31), more than the monthly rent, and 17 of 31 days bills $1,014.56 against 1850 x 17 / 31 = $1,014.52. $2,195 for 31 of 31 days bills $2,195.11. The only shipped test of a 31-day month uses $1,550, which divides exactly. A blank or 0 'days in month' passes the page guard ('0' is a truthy string) and is silently replaced by 30.
evidence.completeness: README features checked: deposit settlement (works), refund vs balance owed (works), unlabelled-deduction flag (works), jurisdiction note (works), prorated rent (works, with the rounding defect), formatItemizedStatement with disclaimer and '(description needed)' (works, tested), optional interest (works), clipboard fallback textarea (code present), usage counting with DNT/GPC and opt-out (usage.test.mjs passes). Not implemented although a page says so: the copy button never disables after an edit, and a day count without a rate is not flagged (vs-a-spreadsheet.html lines 61-65, 86). No stubs or dead links in the four pages; served copy clean.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' from the subject dir: 65 pass, 0 fail. Seeded 6 mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (interest /365 -> /360, interest dropped from refund, days-occupied cap removed), 3 survived (default 30 -> 31 days, balance-owed finding threshold 0 -> 100, and amount > 0 -> >= 0, the last an equivalent mutant because zero amounts are filtered next). The test suite did not catch the proration overcharge because its 31-day case was chosen to divide evenly.
evidence.craft: Read calculator.mjs (229 lines), index.html module script, usage.mjs, all four test files. Small, pure, documented functions. Defects: user-typed deduction descriptions are interpolated into innerHTML unescaped (index.html:268, and into a value attribute at :243), so a description containing '<' or a quote breaks the table row (self-only, nothing is shared); money() is duplicated between calculator.mjs and index.html; silent numeric fallbacks (days in month 0 -> 30, blank days occupied -> 0 with no finding); negative amounts are dropped without a finding, so a credit (prepaid last month, a final-month proration credit) cannot be entered.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, not-legal-advice and privacy lines present on all four pages and in the copied statement (page.test.mjs). README and index claims are backed by calculator.mjs. Interest-state list on index.html checked against statute: NY GOL 7-103(2-a) six-or-more-unit rule confirmed from nysenate.gov text; MA, NJ (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19), CT (C.G.S. 47a-22) and MD (Real Prop. 8-203) from knowledge, all real interest states. Unbacked: vs-a-spreadsheet.html says the copy button 'disables itself if you edit an input without recalculating' (no such code in index.html) and that 'a day count with no rate' is flagged (computeDepositInterest only flags rate without days). calculator.mjs:132 asserts 'Most jurisdictions require a separate written demand to collect a balance beyond the deposit' with no source; a landlord can generally sue in small claims for the excess.
evidence.fitness: Walked the landlord job: deposit $1,500, two deductions, copy statement -> a usable plain-text list. But the job a property manager actually has is a compliant statement on time, and the tool asks for day counts instead of dates (move-in, move-out, lease start), so it cannot say how many days remain before the CA 21 / NY 14 / TX 30 day deadline, cannot compute days held for interest, and the statement carries no property address, tenant name, move-out date or statement date, which is what proves timeliness in NY where lateness forfeits the whole deposit. Credits against the deposit (prepaid rent, interest already paid annually) cannot be entered. A tenant checking a landlord's letter can verify the subtraction.
evidence.domain: Compared with CA Civ. Code 1950.5 (from knowledge; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and law.justia.com both 403 through the proxy), NY GOL 7-108(1-a)(e) (fetched from nysenate.gov: 'Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated ... If a landlord fails ... the landlord shall forfeit any right to retain any portion of the deposit'), NY GOL 7-103 (fetched: 1% per annum administration fee), TX Prop. Code 92.103/92.104/92.107/92.109 (statutes.capitol.texas.gov is a JS app, cited from knowledge: 30 days after surrender, written description and itemized list, forwarding address precondition, bad-faith liability of $100 + 3x the wrongfully withheld amount + fees). The tool ships no state data and says so plainly, which is the honest choice, but it therefore models none of the rules a practitioner checks first: deadlines, CA receipt threshold ($125), deposit caps (CA one month since 2024-07-01 under AB 12; NY one month), NY's 1% admin fee netting, or MD's six-month accrual intervals. Simple interest at days/365 is a reasonable default. Proration uses only the actual-days-in-month method (a 30-day or 365-day annual convention needs the user to type 30 or to precompute), and rounds the daily rate first, which no lease convention calls for when it exceeds the monthly rent.

defects.what: Prorated rent rounds the daily rate to cents before multiplying, so a full 31-day month at $1,850 bills $1,850.08 (more than the monthly rent) and 17 of 31 days bills $1,014.56 instead of $1,014.52; a tenant charged this has an overcharge on paper.

vs-a-spreadsheet.html claims the copy button 'disables itself if you edit an input without recalculating'; index.html has no such listener, so after an edit the copy still hands out the previous settlement.
vs-a-spreadsheet.html claims a day count with no interest rate is flagged; computeDepositInterest only flags a rate with no days, so 400 days held and a blank rate returns 0 interest with no finding.

No dates are collected (move-out, lease start), so the tool cannot count down the itemization deadline (CA Civ. Code 1950.5(g) 21 days; NY GOL 7-108(1-a)(e) 14 days with forfeiture of the whole deposit; TX Prop. Code 92.103 30 days), cannot derive days held for interest, and the copied statement carries no property, tenant, move-out date or statement date to prove timeliness.
Uncited legal assertion in a finding: 'Most jurisdictions require a separate written demand to collect a balance beyond the deposit'.
Days in month of 0 passes the page guard (the string '0' is truthy) and is silently replaced by 30; a blank days-occupied silently becomes 0 with no finding.
Deduction descriptions are interpolated into innerHTML and an attribute unescaped, so a description with '<' or '"' breaks the row (self-only).
Negative line items are dropped silently, so credits against the deposit (prepaid last month, interest already paid, a final-month proration credit) cannot be entered.

Tests leave the default-days fallback and the balance-owed finding boundary unpinned (two surviving mutants), and the only 31-day proration test uses a rent that divides evenly, which hid the overcharge.

verdict: The deposit arithmetic is right: refund, balance owed and simple interest recompute exactly by hand and against Massachusetts' 5% statutory rate, and the interest-state list (NY six-or-more units under GOL 7-103(2-a), MA, NJ, CT, MD) is accurate. Proration is not: rounding the daily rate first makes a full 31-day month at $1,850 bill $1,850.08, more than the rent, and the one 31-day test was chosen to divide evenly. The comparison page claims two safeguards the code does not have (a copy button that disables after an edit, a flag for days held without a rate). The tool deliberately ships no state rules and says so on every page and in the copied statement, which keeps it honest, but a landlord-tenant attorney's first checks (the 21/14/30-day deadlines in CA, NY and TX, NY's forfeiture, CA's $125 receipt rule, dates on the statement) are left entirely to the user, and with no dates collected it cannot help with any of them. A careful subtraction aid with honest limits; not something a property manager would sign a statement off on unaided.
